title: 1954 Guatemalan coup d'etat
summary: In June 1954 Guatemalan president Jacobo Arbenz Guzman was overthrown in a coup orchestrated by the US Central Intelligence Agency and carried out by exiled Colonel Carlos Castillo Armas. Washington feared communist influence, and Arbenz's land reform had hurt the United Fruit Company. The CIA operation, codenamed PBSUCCESS, was documented in records released in 1997 and 2003.

uncertainty.note: Opened sources give "June 1954" for the overthrow. Day-level start of the invasion was not confirmed on an opened page.

where.historical_name: Guatemala City, capital of the Republic of Guatemala

importance.justification: A landmark Cold War covert intervention that ended Guatemala's reform government and shaped Latin American views of US policy.

beats.caption: Arbenz's Decree 900 agrarian reform law was promulgated, hitting the United Fruit Company hardest.
A CIA-orchestrated coup, carried out by exile Colonel Castillo Armas, overthrew Arbenz.
Arbenz's presidency ended, and the CIA later released many redacted records on the operation.
